battle.name: 江陵之戰
battle.brief: 端平三年（一二三六）冬，蒙古軍連下襄樊等城後順漢水南下，在枝江、監利造木筏渡江直趨江陵。宋將孟珙節制四郡軍馬往援，以晝夜變旗、夜間沿江舉火疑兵遲敵，待其營陣既定便連夜出擊，連破二十四寨，奪回被俘將士二萬餘人，蒙古軍北撤，襄樊等城復宋。攻城序列中，配重投石車是壓制城頭的遠程火力。

kit.name: 配重投石車
kit.history: 配重投石車屬於攻城體系中的遠程拋射兵器，通常部署於圍城陣線或防線後方，以石彈打擊城牆、塔樓及集結部隊，支援地面部隊推進。

countries: 江陵之戰是端平三年（一二三六）蒙古帝國第二次南征宋境之役中，蒙古帝國與南宋在京湖防線上的一場攻防。蒙古方面由大汗窩闊台在河南、關中兩線作戰的同時，於江漢方向投入東路大軍：宗王闊出領襄唐鄧之眾，漢人降軍、契丹降軍與蒙古本部兵分擔攻城與守備兩種任務，回回籍與西域來的砲手、工匠編在攻城序列之中，負責配重投石車、撞車與雲梯的操作；漢地降軍充當守備與工程隊伍，蒙古本部兵擔任騎射機動與封鎖江面水路。指揮上，蒙古各宗王分道而進，互不統屬，遇事多請大汗決斷，江陵一路在闊出病後改由忒木台接替。南宋方面以京湖制置司為總樞，長江中游沿岸的襄、鄂、江陵三鎮屯重兵，江陵為荊南軍府，節制司與知州衙門管轄城防；此次救援由孟珙節制蘄州、黃州、光州、信陽四郡軍馬，江北的民兵與隨軍丁壯被編入水陸兩線。蒙古軍此前已連下襄、樊、隨、郢、棗陽、德安等城，江陵告急，荊北門戶洞開。雙方的指揮系統差異甚大：蒙古靠宗王分統加工程技術補位，宋廷靠制置司節制加文官統兵，江陵一役正是這兩種體系在城下的直接對撞。
countriesEn: The Battle of Jiangling was a clash between the Mongol Empire and Southern Song on the Jinghu defensive line during the Mongol Empire's second invasion of Song territory in Duanping 3 (1236). On the Mongol side, while the Great Khan Ogedei was engaged in Henan and Guanzhong, a large eastern force was committed to the middle Yangtze: the prince Ko-chu led the troops from Xiang, Tang and Deng, while surrendered Han Chinese and Khitan troops, Mongol native cavalry, and sling crews and craftsmen from the Muslim and Central Asian regions were divided between assault and garrison duty, the latter handling the counterweight trebuchets, battering rams and siege ladders. Han Chinese surrendered units served as garrison and work parties, while the Mongol native horse carried out manoeuvre and sealed off the river routes. In command the Mongol khans led separate columns without a unified chain of command and referred major decisions to the Great Khan, and after Ko-chu fell ill the drive against Jiangling was taken over by Temur. On the Song side the Jinghu Military Commission was the overall authority, with heavy garrisons at Xiangyang, Ezhou and Jiangling along the middle Yangtze; Jiangling was the seat of the Jingnan military administration, and its defences were handled by the commission and the prefectural office. The relief force in this battle was led by Meng Gong, who took charge of the troops of the four circuits of Qi, Huang, Guang and Xinyang, while the local militia and camp followers were folded into both the land and the river lines. The Mongols had already taken Xiang, Fan, Suizhou, Yingzhou, Zaoyang and De'an, so Jiangling was in danger and the northern Jing gateway stood wide open. The two command systems differed sharply: the Mongols combined khans in independent command with engineering specialists to fill the gaps, while the Song relied on a commission of civil officials directing military units, and Jiangling was a direct collision of those two systems before the walls.
people: 蒙古一方的關鍵人物是闊出。他是蒙古宗王，一二三五年奉命率軍攻唐、鄧，一二三六年三月乘樊城與襄陽相繼陷落之勢收取荊北，四月取隨州、郢州與荊門軍，八月破棗陽軍，德安府亦於同年陷落、守將高達力拒城破殉節，宋人在漢水與沮漳之間的據點被連成一片；十月，闊出病死軍中，窩闊台遂命忒木台接率大軍南下攻江陵，他本人未能見到江陵城下。蒙古軍中另有漢人降將郭侃一類人物，把中原的攻城法與西域工藝帶入蒙古軍的攻城序列，配重投石車的操作與修補主要靠這批受過漢地工匠訓練的人。宋方居首者是孟珙（一一九五至一二四六，字玉汝，父孟宗政原為岳飛部將、鎮隨州多年，一二三四年病卒），端平三年以湖北副都統制總領荊襄軍務、翌年升京湖制置使，此時實際節制蘄、黃、光、信陽四郡軍馬；他不帶主力先渡江，而是先遣民兵部將張順率人渡江，自率大軍殿後，抵枝江、監利一線後才施以夜襲，破了蒙古軍二十四寨，奪回被俘將士與隨軍丁壯二萬餘人。前線其他要角包括襄樊陷落時降元的守將呂文煥、與孟珙同在荊襄一線收復失地的趙範，以及江陵城中的守軍將佐與沿江民兵首領；後者姓名多不見於傳記，只在宋史孟珙傳等篇目中以部將、民兵概括。
peopleEn: The key figure on the Mongol side was Ko-chu, a Mongol prince. In 1235 he was ordered to attack Tang and Deng, and in 1236 he took advantage of the fall of Fancheng and Xiangyang to take over northern Jing in March, seized Suizhou, Yingzhou and Jingmen Army in April, and breached Zaoyang Army in August, while De'an Prefecture also fell that year after a stubborn defence by its commander Gao Da, who died with the city; the Song strongholds between the Han and Juzhang rivers were thus drawn into one connected arc. In October Ko-chu died of illness in the field, and Ogedei ordered Temur to carry on southward against Jiangling, so the prince himself never saw the walls of the city. Among the Mongol forces were men such as Guo Kan, a Chinese defector who brought Central Plain siegecraft and western technologies into the Mongol assault column; the operation and repair of the counterweight trebuchets depended above all on men trained in the Han Chinese craft guilds. The leading figure on the Song side was Meng Gong (1195-1246, courtesy name Yuru, whose father Meng Zongzheng had been a former subordinate of Yue Fei and held Suizhou for many years until his death in 1234). In Duanping 3 he took overall command of the Jingxiang army as deputy commander of Hubei and was promoted the following year to Military Commissioner of Jinghu, and at this time he actually controlled the troops of the four circuits of Qi, Huang, Guang and Xinyang. He did not cross the river with his main body but first sent the militia commander Zhang Shun across to probe the enemy, and led the main force in the rear himself; on reaching the line of Zhijiang and Jianli he struck at night, broke twenty-four Mongol camps in succession, and recovered more than twenty thousand captured soldiers and camp followers. Other names around the front include Lu Wenhuan, the Song commander at Xiangyang who surrendered when the city fell, Zhao Fan, who worked with Meng Gong on the Jingxiang line to recover the lost cities, and the Song officers and militia leaders in Jiangling itself; the latter are rarely named in the histories and appear only as commanders and militia in passages such as the biography of Meng Gong in the Song History.
kits: 本卡的兵器是配重投石車，在這場戰役裡屬於蒙古軍攻城序列中的遠程拋射器械。配重式投石車自十一世紀起在中亞成形，十二世紀經西亞傳入歐洲，以長臂末端懸吊配重、靠墜落與擺動把石彈甩出，拋程遠、落點準，攻城時用來打擊城牆、塔樓與城頭的集結人群。宋人稱蒙古人所用者為回回砲，宋史記載蒙古攻城時曾以配重投石車所擲石彈擊中樊城頭的守將，可見宋將對這類砲具印象之深；元史於蒙古初攻河南、蔡州一線始記回回砲「發石重逾百斤，響如雷霆」，是這類配重砲具規格的早期文字記錄。蒙古軍的攻城裝備是成套的：配重投石車負責遠程壓制，撞車撞擊城門與牆根，雲梯與攻城塔供人登城，望車用於觀察城內外，壕溝中另埋火藥爆炸物，宋人稱之為震天雷，蒙古在北方攻城時已用過此法；石彈、木料與繩索靠隨軍工匠就地製作與運送。守城的宋軍則以角弓、神臂弓、麻札弩壓制牆頭射手，配石砲、擂木與火箭應對雲梯與撞車，江陵與鄂州之間的糧秣又靠漢水漕運北運。配重投石車本身的技術來路也值得一提：它自中亞成形、經西亞傳入歐洲，十二世紀已見於歐洲圍城，蒙古西征後又隨蒙古軍東來與漢地技術合流，到一二六八年蒙古攻阿勒頗時仍用配重投石車攻城。與此同時，把蒙古軍真正推到江陵城下的另一件器材是木筏：蒙古軍在枝江、監利一帶砍伐木料、編造木筏，準備循長江北岸南下，渡江直趨江陵。木筏與配重投石車一同出現，反映出蒙古軍把遠程火力與水上機動並列使用的思路；而孟珙的應對，同樣建立在對這兩樣東西的判斷之上。
kitsEn: The weapon on this card is the counterweight trebuchet, which in this battle belonged to the far-range artillery arm of the Mongol siege train. The counterweight trebuchet took shape in Central Asia in the eleventh century and reached Europe through Persia in the twelfth; a long arm carrying a suspended counterweight was swung by the fall of that weight, flinging a stone to long range and an accurate point of fall, and in siege work it was used to strike walls, towers and troops massed on the parapet. The Song called the Mongols' machines hui-hui pao, and the Song History records that during the siege of Fancheng a stone hurled by a counterweight trebuchet struck a defender on the wall, which shows how deeply the impression of these engines was recorded by Song officers; the Yuan History first records the hui-hui pao with the words that its stones weighed more than a hundred jin and sounded like thunder, in the early attacks on Henan and Caizhou, and that is the earliest written statement of the specification of this kind of counterweight engine. The Mongol siege equipment worked as a set: counterweight trebuchets provided long-range suppression, battering rams struck the gates and the foot of the wall, ladders and siege towers gave men a way up, observation cars were used to watch both inside and outside the walls, and explosive charges buried in trenches, called by the Song the thunder-crash thunderbolt, were used against the foundations, a method the Mongols had already employed in their sieges in the north; stone, timber and rope were cut and lashed on the spot by the engineers who marched with the army. The Song on the walls replied with horn bows, divine-arm crossbows and heavy pellet bows against the archers on the parapet, matched stone cannons, logs and fire arrows against ladders and rams, and the grain for Jiangling and Ezhou was carried north up the Han river. The pedigree of the counterweight trebuchet is worth noting as well: it formed in Central Asia, passed through Persia into Europe and appeared in European sieges in the twelfth century, and after the Mongol westward campaigns it came east again with the Mongol armies and merged with Chinese technique, so that the Mongols were still using counterweight trebuchets when they attacked Aleppo in 1268. At the same time, the other piece of equipment that actually brought the Mongol army to the walls of Jiangling in this battle was the raft: the Mongols felled timber around Zhijiang and Jianli and built rafts, preparing to move down the north bank of the Yangtze and cross over against Jiangling. Rafts and counterweight trebuchets appearing together show how the Mongol command paired long-range fire with river mobility, and Meng Gong's answer rested on exactly the same judgement about these two objects.
tactics: 江陵城下的攻防，重心在江防與渡江點，不在城牆本身。蒙古軍抵江陵後並未立即強攻，而是先在枝江、監利一線造木筏、備舟師，試圖解決渡江問題；配重投石車等攻城器材則擺在能覆蓋城頭與江面泊位的陣地，企圖以遠程火力牽制城內守軍，同時掩護水陸兩線的準備工作。孟珙的應對是一整套以時間換空間的布置：他先派民兵部將張順渡江，試探敵情並牽制；主力則按兵不動，晝夜製造聲勢——白天反覆變換旗幟顏色與軍服，晝夜輪替不絕；夜間沿江高舉火把，綿延數十里，使蒙古軍無法判斷宋軍主力的實數與集結程度；以少示眾的目的，是讓對方疑心援軍已至而不敢遽然渡江，也為自己的夜襲爭取時間。待蒙古軍營陣既定、渡江準備漸成，孟珙集中兵力連夜出擊，一寨一寨地攻破，一連破二十四寨，奪回被擄走的將士與隨軍丁壯二萬餘人；攻守之際不忘毀其器械，以火攻焚燒蒙古營中的攻城器材與積聚，並用鐵索橫江阻其舟師北援與東竄，隨即迫使蒙古軍北撤。攻城方在這一段沒有使用決定性的強攻手段，取勝靠的是情報與判斷；守方則以疑兵、設伏、夜襲的連續動作，把對手的攻勢在渡江之前就拆解掉。
tacticsEn: At Jiangling the centre of the contest lay in the river defence and the crossing points rather than in the walls themselves. After reaching Jiangling the Mongol army did not assault at once, but first built rafts and assembled boats along the line of Zhijiang and Jianli, working out how to get across the river; the siege engines, including the counterweight trebuchets, were set up on ground that could cover the parapet and the moorings on the river, seeking to pin the garrison with long-range fire while masking the preparation of the water and land lines. Meng Gong's answer was a whole scheme of buying time with space. He first sent the militia commander Zhang Shun across the river to test the enemy and keep it occupied, while the main body held still and manufactured the appearance of a great army: by day the banners changed colour and the troops changed clothes in an unbroken rotation; by night torches were raised along the river for tens of li, so that the Mongols could not judge the true size of the Song force or how completely it had assembled. Showing few troops in order to suggest many was meant to make the enemy believe reinforcements had arrived and hesitate to cross, and it also bought the time for the night attack. Once the Mongol camp was fixed and the crossing preparations had ripened, Meng Gong concentrated his troops, struck at night, and took the Mongol encampments one by one, breaking twenty-four in a row and recovering more than twenty thousand captured soldiers and camp followers; in the same stroke he did not forget to destroy the enemy's material, burning the siege engines and stores in the Mongol camp with fire attack and using iron chains drawn across the river to hold off the Mongol boats from reinforcing to the north or breaking away to the east, after which the Mongols were forced to withdraw north. The besieging side used no decisive assault in this stretch, and the victory came from intelligence and judgement, while the defenders dismantled the enemy's offensive before it ever reached the river.
data: 關於兵力與戰果，現存記載多以概括語句出現，只能取其可確證的部分。端平三年（一二三六）蒙古對宋的攻勢由多路同時展開，東路自唐、鄧南下，三月收取襄陽，四月取隨州、郢州與荊門軍，八月破棗陽軍，德安府同年在守將高達力拒之後陷落，宋人在荊北一線連失九州，江陵遂告急；十一月蒙古軍又陷潭州，江西、江南一線同時告急。十月闊出病死，蒙古軍由忒木台率領再度南下，前後兵力的具體數目不見於史文，只知其足以在荊襄、江漢兩地展開攻城與渡江的同時作業。決戰的戰果有較具體的記載：宋軍連破蒙古營寨二十四座，奪回被俘將士與隨軍丁壯二萬餘人；孟珙所部依記載為節制蘄、黃、光、信陽四郡軍馬，數目亦無明載。地理上的距離可以估算：江陵距枝江、監利各數十里，控江處正當長江中游，冬季水落洲渚外露，木筏可近岸；孟珙夜間沿江燃起的火把被記為綿延數十里。時間上，這一戰在端平三年十月進行，蒙古軍在突破受阻後北撤，孟珙隨即與趙範乘勢收復襄、樊、郢、復、江陵一帶失地（各城收復的先後次序，各家繫年略有出入）。攻城砲的規格在宋人記述中可見一端：蒙古攻城所用的配重投石車所擲石彈重逾百斤，響如雷霆，能擊中城頭守將；其餘如石彈確切重量、拋程，未有可靠數字流傳。
dataEn: On numbers and results the surviving records are mostly phrased in summary form, so only what can be firmly supported can be taken from them. In Duanping 3 (1236) the Mongol offensive against Song was opened on several axes at once, the eastern column coming down from Tang and Deng, taking Xiangyang in March, Suizhou, Yingzhou and Jingmen Army in April, and breaching Zaoyang Army in August, with De'an Prefecture falling that same year after a stubborn defence by its commander Gao Da, after which the Song lost nine prefectures along the northern Jing line and Jiangling was in danger; in November the Mongol army also took Tanzhou, and the Jiangxi and Jiangnan lines were in alarm at the same time. In October Ko-chu died of illness and the Mongol army under Temur advanced south again; the exact size of the force is not recorded, only that it was large enough to carry out siege operations and a river crossing simultaneously along the Jingxiang and Jianghan lines. The results of the decisive action are more precisely recorded: the Song broke twenty-four Mongol camps in succession and recovered more than twenty thousand captured soldiers and camp followers. The Song force, described as the troops of the four circuits of Qi, Huang, Guang and Xinyang under Meng Gong, is likewise without a stated headcount. Distances can be estimated: Jiangling lies several tens of li from Zhijiang and Jianli respectively and commands the middle Yangtze, where the winter low water exposes the sandbanks and lets the rafts come close inshore; the torches raised along the river at night by Meng Gong's men are recorded as running for tens of li. In time the battle was fought in the tenth month of Duanping 3, the Mongols withdrew north after being checked, and Meng Gong at once took advantage of the withdrawal with Zhao Fan to recover the lost cities around Xiang, Fan, Yingzhou, Fu and Jiangling, though the sources differ slightly on the order in which the cities were retaken. One end of the specification of the siege engines is visible in the Song account: the stones hurled by the Mongols' counterweight trebuchets weighed more than a hundred jin, sounded like thunder, and could strike defenders on the wall; for the exact weight of the stones and the range of the engines, no reliable figures have come down.
cause: 打起來的原因是蒙古在北方得手之後，把南進的時間表提前了。蒙古第一次南征（一二二六至一二二八年）在江淮一線受挫，江淮以北的宋土反而成了蒙古的策源地，雙方此後二十年以邊界消耗為主。一二三四年金朝覆亡，蒙古失去北方的主要敵手；同年宋蒙議和，宋廷納銀二十萬兩、絹二十萬匹並出犒軍銀，蒙古取得借道攻宋與攻蜀之利，雙方的默契隨即破裂。一二三五年窩闊台乘勝分兵三路攻宋：自將主力循汴水流域南下、經河南趨荊襄，一路入蜀，另一路經湖北南下趨湖南江西，東線則以闊出領襄唐鄧之眾，圖取襄樊，再順漢水下巴江漢。江陵是這盤棋上的關鍵一格：它據長江中游，北控荊山與沮漳之水，南接洞庭與武昌，東可以援鄂，西可以聯蜀；襄樊一旦失守，江陵的城防就直接暴露在蒙古的進攻線上。三月襄陽收降、四月隨郢荊門、八月棗陽與德安一路傳捷，江陵的守軍與朝議都清楚，若江陵再陷，荊襄防線會整段崩潰，蒙古軍即可沿江直取鄂州與江東。朝廷於是急命孟珙率四郡軍馬往援；此前朝中已有人主張南遷避敵，荊襄前線的主張則是固守荊鄂、以江為塹，救援的時機、兵力的分配與渡江的部署，都由此決定。
causeEn: The reason the fighting started was that after the Mongols won out in the north they moved up the timetable for their advance to the south. The first Mongol invasion of Song, from 1226 to 1228, had been checked in the Jianghuai region, and Song territory north of the river became a source of supplies and men for the Mongols, so that for the next twenty years the two sides mainly wore each other down along the border. With the fall of the Jin dynasty in 1234 the Mongols lost their principal enemy in the north; in that same year Song and Mongol concluded a peace under which the Song paid twenty thousand taels of silver, two hundred thousand bolts of silk and a bonus payment for the troops, while the Mongols obtained the right to pass through Song territory and to attack Shu, and the understanding between the two sides broke down at once. In 1235 Ogedei split his forces into three columns against Song: the main force with the Great Khan himself moved down the Bian river and through Henan towards Jingxiang, one column entered Shu, another moved down through Hubei towards Hunan and Jiangxi, while the eastern line under Ko-chu struck at Xiang, Tang and Deng, aiming at Xiangyang and then down the Han river towards the middle Yangtze. Jiangling was the key square on that board: it sits on the middle Yangtze, controls Jing mountain and the waters of the Juzhang to the north, touches Dongting and Wuchang to the south, can support Ezhou to the east and connect with Shu to the west. Once Xiangyang fell, the defences of Jiangling lay directly on the Mongol line of attack. The news of Xiangyang in March, of Suizhou, Yingzhou and Jingmen in April, and of Zaoyang and De'an in August made it plain to the Song command and to the court that if Jiangling were lost the whole Jingxiang line would collapse and the Mongols could ride the river down to Ezhou and Jiangdong. The court therefore ordered Meng Gong with the troops of the four circuits to the rescue. Even before this there had been voices in the capital arguing for a move of the court further south, while the Jingxiang front argued for holding Jing and Ezhou and using the river as a moat; the timing of the relief, the distribution of troops and the deployment of the crossing were all decided within that argument.
impact: 江陵一線守住，對南宋是一次有限度的成功，效果卻超出戰役本身。蒙古東路在長江中游受挫，一時無法順流而下，荊襄與京湖兩線得以重整：孟珙得以利用對手的退兵，與趙範一同收復襄、樊、郢、復、江陵等城，把被蒙古奪去的荊北屏障重新拿回手中，襄樊此後又撐了數十年，直到一二六七年之後蒙古再傾國力來攻，才重演襄樊的陷落；一二三九年蒙古第二次深入荊北、進圍團風大埡寨又被宋軍守住，一二四〇年蒙古軍北返，荊襄線的拉鋸就這樣延續下去。江陵的守禦經驗也進入南宋的城防學：孟珙所部在沿江一線修城築壘、編民兵、造舟師、設烽燧，把江防從幾座孤立的州城連成一條可以互相照應的防線，這套做法後來在鄂州、廬州一線沿用。對蒙古而言，江陵受挫是一次關於渡江的教訓：遠程砲火可以壓制城頭，卻不能解決從上游把大軍渡到南岸的問題，此後蒙古在江漢一線的攻勢改以長期圍城與改道並行，直到後來鄂州與潭州的戰事才打開缺口。與此同時，西路蒙古軍同期深入四川，蜀中州縣次第失守，同年十一月蒙古軍又陷潭州，江南方向的戰線同樣告急——西部與江南的崩解並沒有因為荊襄的得守住而停止，這場江陵的勝利只是把蒙古的腳步拖慢，並沒有改變它三路並進的整體攻勢。
impactEn: Holding the Jiangling line was a limited success for the Song, but its effect went beyond the battle itself. The eastern Mongol thrust on the middle Yangtze was checked and for the time could not ride the river downward, giving the Jingxiang and Jinghu lines room to reform: Meng Gong was able to use the enemy's withdrawal to recover Xiang, Fan, Yingzhou, Fu and Jiangling together with Zhao Fan, taking back the Jingbei barrier the Mongols had seized, and Xiangfan would hold for another several decades, until after 1267 the Mongols again committed the resources of the realm to the same objective and the fall of Xiangfan was reenacted; in 1239 the Mongols came deep into northern Jing a second time and were held off by the Song at Dayi village of Tuanfeng, and in 1240 the Mongol army withdrew north, so the seesaw on the Jingxiang line continued in this way. The lessons of holding Jiangling also entered the Song study of fortification: under Meng Gong the line along the river was walled and embanked, the militia were organised, boats built and beacon fires raised, turning a number of isolated prefectures into a defensive belt that could support one another, a practice later followed at Ezhou and Luzhou. For the Mongols, Jiangling was a lesson about river crossings: long-range artillery could pin the parapet but could not solve the problem of bringing a great army across a great river, and afterwards the Mongol offensive in the Jianghan region was carried out by long siege and by turning the route as well, until the breach came at Ezhou and Tanzhou. At the same time the western Mongol column was pushing deep into Sichuan and the prefectures of Shu fell one after another, and in November of the same year the Mongol army took Tanzhou as well, so the Jiangnan line was in alarm too: the collapse in the west and in the south was not stopped by the fact that Jingxiang held, and the victory at Jiangling only slowed the Mongols down without changing the general offensive they had opened on three axes.
result: 江陵之戰以宋軍的戰術勝利告終：孟珙所部連破二十四寨，奪回被俘將士與隨軍丁壯二萬餘人，蒙古軍北撤，兩軍重新隔江對峙；荊北此前失陷的城池隨後由孟珙、趙範陸續收復，江陵與襄、樊重回宋軍手中，江防與漢水漕運重新接上。這一場勝負在當時被看成京湖防線的一次大捷，朝廷的遷都之議因此暫時收斂，荊襄前線得以繼續維持。戰果的邊界同樣清楚：蒙古在江陵城下並未受到重創，退走的是遠征大軍而不是潰散之師；蒙古軍在華中與江西的攻勢亦未停止，同年十一月便陷潭州，蜀中州縣同期相繼失守，荊北失地雖經收復，但要長久守住仍要再築城壘、置弩砲、編民兵。從整場戰爭的走向看，江陵的勝負沒有改變蒙古滅宋的總目標，只是推遲了它：荊襄線此後仍以襄樊為焦點，四川在另一條戰線上被迅速攻陷，江南的門戶最後還是在一二七〇年代從鄂州方向被撬開。對孟珙本人，這場勝利鞏固了他在南宋軍界的地位，他翌年升任京湖制置使，得以整頓荊襄軍制、推行民兵與屯田之策；對配重投石車而言，它再次證明遠程拋射兵器能決定城頭的進退，卻決定不了大河的走向——攻城器材在江陵的結局，最終仍要由渡江的成敗來裁決。
resultEn: The Battle of Jiangling ended in a tactical victory for the Song: Meng Gong's troops broke twenty-four camps in succession and recovered more than twenty thousand captured soldiers and camp followers, the Mongol army withdrew north, and the two sides faced each other across the water again; the cities of northern Jing that had been lost were then recovered one after another by Meng Gong and Zhao Fan, Jiangling and Xiangfan returned to Song hands, and the river defence and the Han river transport were joined up once more. At the time the result was treated in the capital as a great victory for the Jinghu line, the argument for moving the court south was set aside for the moment, and the Jingxiang front could be maintained. The limits of the result were equally clear: the Mongols were not badly hurt before Jiangling, and it was a field army that withdrew rather than a routed one; the Mongol offensive in central China and in Jiangxi did not stop either, for they took Tanzhou in November of the same year, while the prefectures of Shu were falling in turn, and although the lost ground in northern Jing was recovered, holding it for long still required new walls and embankments, crossbows on platforms and organised militia. Seen in the wider course of the war, the outcome at Jiangling did not change the Mongol aim of destroying Song, it only delayed it. The Jingxiang line continued to turn on Xiangyang, Sichuan was broken down quickly on another front, and the gateway to the south was finally forced open in the 1270s from the direction of Ezhou. For Meng Gong himself the victory confirmed his standing in the Song military; he was made Military Commissioner of Jinghu the following year and was able to reorganise the Jingxiang army system and press the policies of militia and garrison farms; for the counterweight trebuchet it was a further demonstration that far-range engines can decide the fate of a parapet but cannot decide the course of a great river, and in the end the artillery at Jiangling was still judged by whether the crossing succeeded.
